row_statement: Conjecture 6.4 of Aragao, Chapman, Ortega and Souza (the interval Schur number I(r) equals the Schur number S(r) for all r) is false at r = 4: every 4-colouring of {2,...,89} has a monochromatic solution of x + y = z, which by scaling gives I(4) <= 89/2, while the classical colouring of {1,...,44} gives S(4) >= 45. The exact value of I(4) is not determined.

round2-final-check-360964-sol61-20261120-r1/FINAL-REVIEW-360964.md (GPT-6.1 Sol: PASS; COUNTS; no definition issue; the proved bound 44.5 suffices)
caveats: The source proved 41 <= I(4) <= 45 and said it had not settled whether I(4) = S(4); the first grid finer than the integers, at the first open number of colours, already decides it. Easy to find, laborious to certify: the kernel-checked certificate has 184,658 steps.
The Opus review computed the sharper bound I(4) <= 42 by SAT; Lean proves only I(4) <= 44.5, which is enough.
The endpoint quantifies over r >= 1, the source's reading; S(4) is proved to be a genuine minimum, so no default value does the work.
